name_reason: Compliant fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '49' is the dispatch-table index 0x49 (entry @ 0x51CB5), a meaningful domain ID, not an address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_sentinel' to '__ch29_dragon_down_1': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path -- ch29 char_spawn_record[0] = a defense-core dragon (enemy_data 36, char_id 0x68, lv30) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x49, so the dragon's death dispatches consequence[0x49], setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x12]=1 to mark this dragon destroyed (one of the ch29 3-dragon objective flags 0x12/0x13/0x14 set by 0x49/0x4D/0x4E). The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path; the tail it borrows is ch28's handler_44 code, but the flag semantics here are ch29's dragon marker.
purpose: Chapter 29 defense-core-dragon progress marker (dispatch slot 0x49, reached via the ch29 kill-drop path when the dragon record[0] enemy_data 36, pickup_kind=2 param=0x49, falls): marks this dragon destroyed by setting tile_event_consumed_flags[0x12] = 1 (one of the 3-dragon objective flags), with no other side effects.
logic_summary: Single statement: store 1 into tile_event_consumed_flags[0x12]. In the binary it is a 10-byte stub (PUSH 4; CALL __CHK; JMP 0x35AAE) that borrows the Class-3 shared consume-slot-0x12 tail (MOV EAX,[consumed_flags_ptr]; MOV byte [EAX+0x12],1; RET) hosted at the end of fd2_chapter_event_handler_44__ch28_dialog_with_state @ 0x35A48 (alt_66 @ 0x35AAE). The __CHK(4) is the Watcom stack-probe prologue and carries no source-level semantics. Slot 0x12 is the prerequisite that the handler_44/handler_45 chain depends on. event_arg is never read.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Dispatch-table ABI arg word (1-arg cdecl void fn(uint event_arg)); not read by this handler.
params.reason: Appropriate generic name for the unused dispatch-table ABI argument; not an address residue. Matches the convention used across the whole handler family for handlers that ignore the arg.

writes_globals: data_fd2_field_map_tile_event_consumed_flags_ptr (writes through the pointer: consumed_flags[0x12] = 1; the pointer global itself, at 0x53AD5, is read not written)
comment_original_issue: Source comment previously stated the slot was unreferenced and framed flag[0x12] as 'the ch28 sentinel scene slot'. Corrected: LIVE via the ch29 kill-drop path (record[0] dragon pickup_kind=2 param=0x49); flag[0x12] is a ch29 dragon-progress marker (the ch28 reference is only the borrowed code tail).
